solution: The height is the shadow times \(\tan 60^\circ\): \(16 \times \sqrt{3} = 16\sqrt{3}\) m.
The ships are \(h \cot 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}h\) and \(h \cot 45^\circ = h\) from the base, on opposite sides. The distance between them is \((\sqrt{3} + 1)h\).

From the bottom of the building the elevation is \(60^\circ\), so the distance is \(\frac{75}{\sqrt{3}} = 25\sqrt{3}\) m. From the top it is \(30^\circ\), so the tower rises \(25\sqrt{3} \tan 30^\circ = 25\) m above the building, which is \(75 - 25 = 50\) m tall.
At \(45^\circ\) the distance equals the building's height \(H\). Then \(\tan 60^\circ = \frac{H + 100}{H} = \sqrt{3}\), so \(H = \frac{100}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = 50(\sqrt{3} + 1)\) m.
The tower is \(15 \tan 30^\circ = 5\sqrt{3}\) m tall. At \(60^\circ\) its shadow is \(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 5\) m.
When the shadow equals the height, the tangent of the elevation is 1, so the angle is \(45^\circ\).

The horizontal distances are \(\cot 60^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) km and \(\cot 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}\) km, so the plane covers \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) km in 10 s. Its speed is \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \times 360 = 240\sqrt{3}\) km/h.

The fruit is \(\frac{10}{3} - 2 = \frac{4}{3}\) m above his height, at a horizontal distance of \(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\) m. The angle has \(\tan\theta = \frac{4/3}{4/\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(\theta = 30^\circ\).

value: h tan a / (tan b - tan a)
solution: With tower height \(H\), the distance is \(H \cot\alpha\), and \(H + h = H \cot\alpha \tan\beta\). So \(H(\tan\beta - \tan\alpha) = h\tan\alpha\) and \(H = \frac{h \tan\alpha}{\tan\beta - \tan\alpha}\).
The street is \(h \cot\phi\) wide, from the depression of the foot. The top is \(h \cot\phi \tan\theta\) above the window, so the house is \(h[\tan\theta \cot\phi + 1]\) high.

note: checked: p = s cot a, q = s cot 3a
solution: \(p = s \cot\alpha\) and \(q = s \cot 3\alpha\), so \(p - q = s\left(\frac{1}{\tan\alpha} - \frac{1}{\tan 3\alpha}\right) = s\left(\frac{\tan 3\alpha - \tan\alpha}{\tan 3\alpha \tan\alpha}\right)\).

From the midpoint, \(\frac{K}{2}\) from each post, the tangents are \(\frac{2h}{K}\) and \(\frac{4h}{K}\). Complementary angles have tangents multiplying to 1, so \(\frac{8h^2}{K^2} = 1\) and \(h = \frac{K}{2\sqrt{2}}\).

The flagstaff's top is at the observer's height, 30 m, so at horizontal distance \(d\) it subtends \(\theta\) with \(\tan\theta = \frac{5}{d}\), and building and flagstaff together subtend \(2\theta\) with \(\tan 2\theta = \frac{30}{d}\). Then \(\frac{10/d}{1 - 25/d^2} = \frac{30}{d}\), so \(d^2 = \frac{75}{2}\) and the distance is \(5\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\) m.
At \(45^\circ\) the tower is 60 m high; at \(30^\circ\) the boat is \(60\sqrt{3}\) m away. It covered \(60(\sqrt{3} - 1) \approx 43.9\) m in 5 s, about \(8.78\) m/s, which is roughly 31.5 km/h.
E and F are on opposite sides, so \(h \cot 60^\circ + h \cot 30^\circ = 160\), that is \(h\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3}\right) = \frac{4h}{\sqrt{3}} = 160\). So \(h = 40\sqrt{3}\) ft.
The standing part is \(20 \tan 30^\circ = \frac{20}{\sqrt{3}}\) m and the broken part \(\frac{20}{\cos 30^\circ} = \frac{40}{\sqrt{3}}\) m. The post was \(\frac{60}{\sqrt{3}} = 20\sqrt{3}\) m high.

With cloud height \(H\) and horizontal distance \(x\), \(H - h = x\tan\beta\) and \(H + h = x\tan\alpha\). Dividing, \(H = h\frac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{\tan\alpha - \tan\beta} = h \sin(\alpha + \beta) \operatorname{cosec}(\alpha - \beta)\).
At \(45^\circ\) the pillar is 100 m high; for \(60^\circ\) it must be \(100\sqrt{3}\) m. It must be raised by \(100(\sqrt{3} - 1)\) m.

With tower height \(h\), the car goes from \(h\sqrt{3}\) to \(h\) away, covering \(h(\sqrt{3} - 1)\) in 12 minutes. The last \(h\) takes \(\frac{12}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = 6(\sqrt{3} + 1) \approx 16.39\) minutes, about 16 min 23 s.
The horizontal distance falls from \(1000\sqrt{3}\) to \(\frac{1000}{\sqrt{3}}\) m, a change of \(\frac{2000}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1154.7\) m in 60 s. The speed is about 19.25 m/s.
If \(\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\), then \(\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}\). The tower is \(20 \times \frac{3}{4} = 15\) m high.

The tangents from the eye make \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) with the line to the centre, so the centre is \(r \operatorname{cosec}\frac{\alpha}{2}\) away. Its height is that distance times \(\sin\beta\): \(r \sin\beta \operatorname{cosec}\frac{\alpha}{2}\).

note: checked: h cot a - h cot b = h/2
solution: The two distances are \(h\cot\alpha\) and \(h\cot\beta\), and they differ by \(\frac{h}{2}\). So \(\cot\alpha - \cot\beta = \frac{1}{2}\).
From \(\cot\alpha - \cot\beta = \frac{1}{2}\) with \(\cot 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), \(\cot\beta = \sqrt{3} - \frac{1}{2}\).
At elevation \(\beta\) the distance is \(h\cot\beta = \frac{h}{4}\).
